subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What should Claude CLI auth epochs treat as the session identity when both an OpenClaw auth profile and local Claude CLI storage are present?
rationale: Current main still invalidates sessions on local file presence even when the profile identity is unchanged, but suppressing that signal changes the auth/session safety boundary and should be an explicit maintainer decision.

options.title: Make profile identity canonical
options.body: When a selected auth-profile credential exists, use it as the epoch identity and fall back to local storage only for bootstrap/local-only cases, with tests for logout and account-switch invalidation.

options.title: Use a host-owned mode
options.body: Land a narrowed host-owned Claude CLI policy only if it also prevents source-presence churn and proves upgrade behavior for existing session bindings.

options.title: Keep storage-presence invalidation
options.body: Close or reject the request if maintainers want any local credential storage-source change to force session reset despite the reported continuity cost.

recommendation.title: Make profile identity canonical
recommendation.body: When a selected auth-profile credential exists, use it as the epoch identity and fall back to local storage only for bootstrap/local-only cases, with tests for logout and account-switch invalidation.

likelyOwner.reason: The key invalidation behavior and central auth-epoch/session files trace to `steipete`, making him the strongest available owner for the policy decision.
